subject: Hosted API annual commit scenarios + transition timeline
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@graphvana.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring annual commit tiers for hosted API

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is evaluating hosted API options for production search and summarization workloads. Before we get legal involved, can you send a short overview of annual commit tier scenarios you offer (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) and the typical per-token discounts at each level?

A few specifics we care about:
- Current usage pattern: bursty inference with daily peaks, roughly 80M tokens/month now rising to ~250M tokens/month projected in 12 months.
- We need clarity on overage rules and downgrade/upgrade windows mid-year.
- Any minimum on-term or PO steps for a mid-market deal.

If you can share an example worksheet with pricing numbers and a suggested transition plan (e.g., how to move between tiers and how credits/overages are handled), that would be ideal. We're hoping to have a procurement conversation the week of Mar 8.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — if easier, happy to take a 30-min call.

Best,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform
Graphvana


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@graphvana.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commit tiers for hosted API

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for the product time. I put together three practical commit scenarios and attached a worksheet that maps projected usage to per-token pricing, overage mechanics, and transition rules (attached: 20270220-commit-scenarios.xlsx). High level:

- Starter: 200M tokens/year, friendly per-token price for early-stage teams, no minimum monthly draw, 10% discount vs list for hosted API. Overage billed at list rates with monthly smoothing options.
- Growth: 1B tokens/year, 18% discount, preferred queueing (improved latency at contention), 90-day upgrade window and prorated credits on downgrades.
- Enterprise: 5B+ tokens/year, 28% discount, SLA-backed latency tiers, dedicated capacity option (opt-in), custom routing and committed burst capacity.

Transition rules (short): upgrades effective immediately with pro-rated billing; downgrades limited to once per quarter with a 30-day notice and available ramp credits for predictable reductions. We included an example 12-month glide path from Starter -> Growth as usage increases.

Next steps: if this looks close to what you need, I can schedule a procurement call for Mar 9 and push an initial term sheet + commit terms PDF for your finance team.

Opening note: the discounts above assume a standard annual commit with net-30 PO. If Graphvana needs upfront crediting or multi-year pricing, we can adjust the effective discount.

I've cc'd Marissa from our pricing team for visibility.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Alex's request and the starter worksheet I drafted. Quick questions:

1) Can we firm up the Growth discount at 20% instead of 18% if Graphvana agrees to a 2x ramp (1B token commit with a 6-month cadence check-in)? That moves us closer to top-of-funnel without giving away Enterprise economics.
2) For downgrades: we proposed quarterly downgrades with ramp credits. Can legal limit frequency to once per quarter but allow one emergency downgrade per year with admin approval?
3) Any objection to offering a one-time onboarding credit (50k token credit) to help during migration?

I expect Alex will push for clearer overage caps (max monthly overage as percentage of committed throughput) — we should provide a modeled example in the term sheet.

Suggested reply to keep momentum: confirm the three scenarios, signal we can be flexible on Growth discount to 20% with the 2x ramp, and propose Mar 9 for procurement call.

— Naomi

Subject: Hosted API annual commit proposal (Graphvana)

Alex — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal pricing and legal guidance together. Attached is a short proposal (commit-terms-draft.pdf) and the committed-scenarios worksheet we discussed. Executive summary below; full details are in the attachments.

Executive summary
- Starter Tier: 240M tokens/year (baseline), effective per-token price = list * 0.90 (10% off). Monthly overage billed at list; 2x smoothing available as an add-on.
- Growth Tier: 1B tokens/year commit with a 20% effective discount (we agreed to 20% if Graphvana signs a 12-month annual commitment and agrees to a 6-month cadence check-in on usage). Upgrades effective immediately; downgrades allowed once per quarter with 30-day notice and prorated ramp credits.
- Enterprise Tier: 5B tokens/year+, 28% discount; includes optional dedicated capacity, SLA credits for latency breaches, and priority routing. Multi-year pricing and upfront credits available on request.

Key commercial items
- Billing: Net 30 with standard PO. Upfront credits (prepaid) available for improved effective pricing and reserved burst capacity.
- Overage & caps: Overage billed monthly at published list rates; we can cap monthly overage to a negotiated percentage of committed throughput (example: 25% cap) if you include a short-term buffer credit.
- Migration support: one-time onboarding credit of 50k tokens and two technical hours of priority onboarding support included in Growth+ signings.

Next steps
1) Review attached term sheet and worksheet — highlight any redlines for legal.
2) If acceptable, schedule procurement call on Mar 9 — proposed time: 10:00 AM PT.
3) Provide the PO or indicate preferred billing cadence; we'll prepare DocuSign for signatures.

If you'd like, we can also model a 3x ramp variant for year 1 (conservative vs aggressive growth paths) — I can send that tonight.

Thanks and looking forward to next steps.

Best,
